definitions.explanation: A soft, rectangular loaf of white bread sold in thick slices, typically 4-, 5-, 6-, or 8-slice cuts. A staple breakfast food in Japan.

examples.japanese: {食|しょく}パンを{一斤|いっきん}{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought one loaf of bread.

examples.japanese: {朝|あさ}は{食|しょく}パンにバターを{塗|ぬ}って{食|た}べる。
examples.english: In the morning I eat toast with butter.

examples.japanese: この{店|みせ}の{食|しょく}パンは{耳|みみ}までやわらかくて{人気|にんき}がある。
examples.english: This shop's bread is popular because it's soft all the way to the crust.

notes:
Short for {主食|しゅしょく}パン (staple bread). Refers specifically to the rectangular white loaf sold at bakeries and supermarkets, as distinct from other bread types like フランスパン (baguette) or {菓子|かし}パン (sweet bread).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {食|しょく}パンを{焼|や}く (toast bread)
- {食|しょく}パンの{耳|みみ} (bread crust — literally "ears")
- {六枚切|ろくまいぎ}りの{食|しょく}パン (bread sliced into six)

In Japan, {食|しょく}パン is typically sold in thicker slices than Western bread. The most popular thickness is {六枚切|ろくまいぎ}り (6 slices per loaf), though {四枚切|よんまいぎ}り (4 slices, thick) is common in the Kansai region.
